findings.message: The plan specifies a WRITE_LOCK for atomic appends to the per-project journal but fails to address cross-process file locking and sharing on Windows when both the dashboard service and CLI tools (e.g., `anchor.py rnd events`) attempt to write to or read the journal concurrently, potentially causing sharing violations or file corruption.

The proposed 'no' branch fallback for PTYs (drain/park/warm-resume) downplays the severity of dashboard restarts. If PTYs remain dashboard-owned, restarting the dashboard will terminate the shell and any active child processes (e.g., SSH, repl, build). A 'warm-resume seed' cannot preserve running process state, resulting in complete state loss rather than a simple 'warm reconnect.'

findings.message: The plan fails to define the mechanism by which the browser obtains the auth cookie. If the GET data plane is default-deny, the browser cannot load the dashboard to prompt the user for a token unless a specific unauthenticated bootstrap/login route is explicitly designed, allowlisted, and secure against token extraction.

It is unclear if the safety gate requires running the walks 20 times in a single night to check for flakes, or soaking them over 20 calendar nights, which would introduce a massive 3-week serialization delay for phase completion.

The plan notes that Mitigation 9 is not cited or mapped to any phase, deferring its reconciliation to Stage 2. findings.section: Phase 4 — Phase 3 — Consolidation & Data Hygiene (C5 + C6)
findings.message: Executing `git rm --cached` on the ~62 tracked runtime artifacts will cause Git to delete those files from the working directory upon pulling/checking out the branch on the live server, destroying active state before the data migration script can run.

On Windows, restarting the supervisor process will break anonymous stdout/stderr pipes shared with spawned child processes, causing those children to crash on subsequent writes and preventing the restarted supervisor from re-attaching to their output streams.

findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 — Declarative Route Table & Default-Deny Auth (C2)
findings.message: Falling back to legacy if-elif chains means the routing is not default-deny by construction during the strangler migration period, exposing the system to auth bypasses for any route not yet explicitly migrated.

Relying exclusively on the 'inline' (in-process) supervisor seam for the test suite means the loopback token-authed IPC protocol and supervisor process boundaries are never covered by automated regression tests.
Replaying journal-ahead 'intent' events blindly to resolve divergence could force mutations that failed or were aborted in the authoritative legacy store, risking database corruption.

findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 — Declarative Route Table & Default-Deny Auth (C2)
findings.message: The draft plan mandates cookie-based browser page navigation when ANCHOR_TOKEN is set, but fails to define the mechanism or route by which this cookie is initially authenticated and set, risking a complete lockout of browser clients.

While the plan asserts that jobs survive a supervisor restart due to job-object breakaway, it does not specify how a restarted supervisor process persists and reconstructs process handles or PIDs to re-attach to and resume monitoring those running jobs.

The plan does not specify the behavior when a journal write fails. If the journal write fails but the legacy store write proceeds, it creates a 'legacy-ahead' divergence that violates the dual-write parity requirement.

The draft contains conflicting phase numbering across section titles (e.g., 'Phase 1 — Phase 0', 'Phase 2 — Phase 1', 'Phase 3 — Phase 2'), which creates ambiguity for the implementation sequence and risks process errors during incremental delivery.
Mitigation 9 is explicitly identified as having no citation or mapping in the phase specifics, leaving an unresolved risk/mitigation gap in the Master Plan before progressing to Stage 2.
